Time: 2 min. Teaching intent: Open the hour and connect it to the week's decision.
Talk track: Distinguish code correctness, physical agreement, calibration, and residual uncertainty.
Expected answer / misconception: Students can name the outcome.
Visual: The visual previews the physical design or evidence chain.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Set the evidence contract.
Talk track: A validation plan naming reference measurements, split cases, error metric, and acceptance rule.
Expected answer / misconception: A named artifact with source and a check, not an unsupported opinion.
Visual: Input, reasoning, and evidence are separate.

R5: NIST, Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing | https://www.nist.gov/publications/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing-standardized-approach

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Does mesh convergence prove package accuracy?
Expected answer / misconception: No. It addresses a numerical question, not the match to physical observations.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Verification asks whether equations and numerical methods were implemented as intended; it is separate from physical agreement. Trace the visual in order: equation; implementation; numerical check. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Refine a mesh or compare a simple analytic benchmark. Even a converged result can be physically wrong if material data are wrong.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Refine a mesh or compare a simple analytic benchmark. Even a converged result can be physically wrong if material data are wrong. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A parameter fitted to one set of measurements must be assessed on independent conditions before broader claims. Trace the visual in order: calibration set; fitted parameter; held-out check. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Fit a stress-free temperature using one coupon, then test a different package or temperature range; preserve the fitted value and data partition.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Material properties, geometry, process history, measurements, and model form each can change a prediction. Trace the visual in order: input uncertainty; model-form limits; measurement error. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: For warpage, list CTE uncertainty, cure-state history, thickness tolerance, fixture influence, and optical measurement uncertainty.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
